correctness.rationale: Derived component color f(u)=u³/(1−2u+2u²) exactly from the Planck factor. Computed fʺ(u)=2u(2u²−6u+3)/(1−2u+2u²)³>0 for 0<u<1/2, so Jensen gives exact lower bound and equality only for coincident temperatures. The exact gap u/2−f(u)=u(1−2u)/(2(1−2u+2u²))>0 proves strict upper bound. A two-point chord varying continuously from the endpoint chord to a degenerate point gives every ordinate between; all constructed temperatures/amplitudes are strictly positive and finite. Two-band data always admit a one-temperature match. Exact rational witness and checker verified from actual local verify.py (4008 assertions). No finite computation used to justify infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Novelty assessed for the exact necessary-and-sufficient three-color region and 2-component completion, not for any known blackbody model, three-flux inverse, color diagram or Jensen convexity. Inspected closest full texts explicitly treat one- versus two-temperature spectral fitting but give no all-positive-parameter sharp global classification, no rational boundary f and no proof that two components realize every interior color. Published-result records were screened for related spectral, Planck, temperature-mixture and color-region formulations; no near overlap was found. Multiple published mathematical-record queries returned unrelated Fourier/convexity results. Priority remains provisional because generic convex-gamut literature may include a specialized equivalent and no independent audit has occurred.
residual_risks: Historical-priority risk: older spectral/color-temperature, color-gamut, radiative-transfer or convex-geometric literature may already specialize the same geometric 1:2:4 Planck curve.
The three-flux isothermal ratio relation itself is prior art, and no originality is claimed for it.
A stronger general theorem about exact convex hulls of Planck color curves, if identified, could imply the entire statement.
Physical relevance depends on known common emissivity index and negligible bandpass/measurement effects; these are scope limitations rather than flaws in the exact model.

value.rationale: A documented astrophysical problem is deciding whether a sparse thermal dust SED is compatible with a single temperature, temperature heterogeneity, or an incorrect emissivity model. The theorem is a natural complete classification, not just a convenient numerical fit: it supplies an exact feasible data domain for any finite number of thermal components, a sharp equality-only single-temperature boundary, an unattainable but optimal upper bound, a universal two-component realization, and sharp impossibility of detection from just two bands. It clarifies precisely what noiseless three-color observations can and cannot infer under a fixed emissivity law; it does not claim empirical observability under noise.
